atoms.1: The treatment of Pelvic Inflammatory Disease (PID) involves a combination of antibiotics.
atoms.2: Antibiotic treatment for PID should provide broad-spectrum coverage of likely etiologic pathogens.
atoms.3: Likely etiologic pathogens for PID include N. gonorrhoeae.
atoms.4: Likely etiologic pathogens for PID include C. trachomatis.
atoms.5: Likely etiologic pathogens for PID include gram-negatives.
atoms.6: Likely etiologic pathogens for PID include anaerobes.
atoms.7: Likely etiologic pathogens for PID include Group B streptococcus.
atoms.8: Likely etiologic pathogens for PID include genital mycoplasmas.
atoms.9: The choice of empirical treatment regimen depends on the severity of symptoms.
atoms.10: The choice of empirical treatment regimen depends on the local epidemiology of sexually transmitted infections.
atoms.11: For mild-to-moderate acute PID, outpatient oral therapy can be considered.
atoms.12: Outpatient oral therapy regimens for mild-to-moderate acute PID can include a cephalosporin (e.g., cefoxitin) plus doxycycline or clindamycin.
atoms.13: Patients who do not respond to oral therapy within 72 hours should be reevaluated.
atoms.14: Patients who do not respond to oral therapy within 72 hours should be administered parenteral therapy.
atoms.15: Parenteral therapy for non-responding patients can be administered on an outpatient basis.
atoms.16: Parenteral therapy for non-responding patients can be administered on an inpatient basis.
atoms.17: For more severe cases of PID, parenteral therapy is recommended.
atoms.18: For cases of PID with severe symptoms, parenteral therapy is recommended.
atoms.19: Options for parenteral therapy include intravenous cefoxitin and doxycycline.
atoms.20: Options for parenteral therapy include clindamycin/gentamicin.
atoms.21: Hospitalization may be considered for patients who require intravenous therapy.
atoms.22: Hospitalization may be considered for patients who have a temperature above 101.0°F (38.3°C).
atoms.23: Hospitalization may be considered for patients who are unable to follow outpatient treatment regimens.
atoms.24: Prevention of long-term complications of PID includes using broad-spectrum antibiotics.
atoms.25: Prevention of long-term complications of PID includes addressing the underlying cause of the infection.
atoms.26: Close follow-up is recommended to prevent reinfection.
atoms.27: Evaluation of male sexual partners is recommended to prevent reinfection.
